module Gopurs.ControlExprs
  ( failure
  , branch
  , booleanAnd
  , booleanOr
  ) where

import Prelude
import Data.Array as Array
import Data.Array.NonEmpty (NonEmptyArray, toArray)
import Data.Foldable (foldl)
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..), fromMaybe)
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (getExprType, unwrapTcoExpr)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, ExprResult, TranslateExpr, StmtTree(..), flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.GoAst (rawGo, GoExpr(..), GoType(..), goTypeToStr)
import Gopurs.GoConversions (coerceGoExpr, unboxGoExpr)
import Gopurs.GoTypes (exprTypeToGoType)
import Gopurs.Printer (printGoExpr)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.CoreFn (ExprType(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendSyntax(Fail), Pair(..))

failure :: ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> String -> ExprResult
failure { metadata, modNameStr, mbExpectedExprType, mbExpectedGoType } nextId tcoExpr msg =
  let
    expectedGoType = fromMaybe inferredGoType mbExpectedGoType
    inferredGoType = exprTypeToGoType metadata.sharedRecords metadata.pointerAdtPaths metadata.enumAdts metadata.elidedCtors modNameStr
      ( case getExprType tcoExpr of
          Any -> fromMaybe Any mbExpectedExprType
          ty -> ty
      )
    expectedGoTypeStr = goTypeToStr expectedGoType
  in
    { stmts: StmtEmpty, expr: rawGo ("func() " <> expectedGoTypeStr <> " { panic(" <> printGoExpr (GoString msg) <> ") }()"), exprType: expectedGoType, nextId }

branch :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> NonEmptyArray (Pair TcoExpr) -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
branch translate context@{ codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr, mbExpectedGoType, options: { isTail } } nextId branches def =
  let
    resDef = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, options = { isTail, inEffectBlock: false } }) nextId def

    computedBranches = foldl
      ( \acc (Pair condExpr bodyExpr) ->
          let
            resCond = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) acc.nextId condExpr
            resBody = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, options = { isTail, inEffectBlock: false } }) resCond.nextId bodyExpr
          in
            { nextId: resBody.nextId, results: acc.results <> [ { cond: resCond, body: resBody } ] }
      )
      { nextId: resDef.nextId, results: [] }
      (toArray branches)

    isFailNode = case unwrapTcoExpr def of
      Fail _ -> true
      _ -> false

    allTypes = (if isFailNode then [] else [ resDef.exprType ]) <> map (\r -> r.body.exprType) computedBranches.results

    hasTypeValue = Array.any
      ( \t -> case t of
          TypeValue -> true
          _ -> false
      )
      allTypes

    -- The consumer fixes the join representation when its ABI is known.
    -- Generic branches adapt at their exit; native branches then avoid a
    -- structural box/unbox round trip through the shared result slot.
    expectedGoType = fromMaybe inferredGoType mbExpectedGoType

    inferredGoType =
      if hasTypeValue then TypeValue
      else
        let
          nubbed = Array.nub (map goTypeToStr allTypes)
        in
          if Array.length nubbed == 1 then fromMaybe TypeValue (Array.head allTypes)
          else TypeValue

    tmpVar = "__t" <> show computedBranches.nextId
    declTmp = StmtLeaf (rawGo ("var " <> tmpVar <> " " <> goTypeToStr expectedGoType))
    labelName = "end_branch_" <> show computedBranches.nextId

    buildIfs = foldl
      ( \acc r ->
          let
            goIf = GoIfElse (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr r.cond.expr r.cond.exprType TypeBool) (flattenStmts r.body.stmts <> [ GoMutate tmpVar (coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr r.body.expr r.body.exprType expectedGoType), rawGo ("goto " <> labelName) ]) []
          in
            acc <> StmtLeaf (rawGo "{") <> r.cond.stmts <> StmtLeaf goIf <> StmtLeaf (rawGo "}")
      )
      StmtEmpty
      computedBranches.results
  in
    { stmts: declTmp <> buildIfs <> StmtLeaf (rawGo "{") <> resDef.stmts <> StmtLeaf (GoMutate tmpVar (coerceGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resDef.expr resDef.exprType expectedGoType)) <> StmtLeaf (rawGo "}") <> StmtLeaf (rawGo (labelName <> ":")), expr: GoVar tmpVar, exprType: expectedGoType, nextId: computedBranches.nextId + 1 }

booleanAnd :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
booleanAnd translate context@{ codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr } nextId e1 e2 =
  let
    res1 = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId e1
    res2 = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) res1.nextId e2
  in
    if isEmptyStmts res2.stmts then
      { expr: GoBinOp "&&" (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res1.expr res1.exprType TypeBool) (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res2.expr res2.exprType TypeBool), exprType: TypeBool, stmts: res1.stmts <> res2.stmts, nextId: res2.nextId }
    else
      let
        tmpVar = "__t_and_" <> show res2.nextId
        declTmp = StmtLeaf (rawGo ("var " <> tmpVar <> " bool = false\nif " <> printGoExpr (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res1.expr res1.exprType TypeBool) <> " {\n"))
        assignTmp = StmtLeaf (rawGo (tmpVar <> " = " <> printGoExpr (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res2.expr res2.exprType TypeBool) <> "\n}"))
      in
        { expr: rawGo tmpVar, exprType: TypeBool, stmts: res1.stmts <> declTmp <> res2.stmts <> assignTmp, nextId: res2.nextId + 1 }

booleanOr :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
booleanOr translate context@{ codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr } nextId e1 e2 =
  let
    res1 = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId e1
    res2 = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) res1.nextId e2
  in
    if isEmptyStmts res2.stmts then
      { expr: GoBinOp "||" (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res1.expr res1.exprType TypeBool) (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res2.expr res2.exprType TypeBool), exprType: TypeBool, stmts: res1.stmts <> res2.stmts, nextId: res2.nextId }
    else
      let
        tmpVar = "__t_or_" <> show res2.nextId
        declTmp = StmtLeaf (rawGo ("var " <> tmpVar <> " bool = true\nif !(" <> printGoExpr (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res1.expr res1.exprType TypeBool) <> ") {\n"))
        assignTmp = StmtLeaf (rawGo (tmpVar <> " = " <> printGoExpr (unboxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr res2.expr res2.exprType TypeBool) <> "\n}"))
      in
        { expr: rawGo tmpVar, exprType: TypeBool, stmts: res1.stmts <> declTmp <> res2.stmts <> assignTmp, nextId: res2.nextId + 1 }

isEmptyStmts :: StmtTree -> Boolean
isEmptyStmts StmtEmpty = true
isEmptyStmts (StmtAppend s1 s2) = isEmptyStmts s1 && isEmptyStmts s2
isEmptyStmts _ = false

module Gopurs.EffectExprs
  ( bindEffect
  , pureValue
  , defer
  , primitive
  , wrap
  , wrapCachedInt
  ) where

import Prelude
import Control.Alternative (guard)
import Data.Map as Map
import Data.Maybe (Maybe(..))
import Data.Tuple (Tuple(..))
import Gopurs.ExprAnalysis (executeIfOpaque, getExprType, isEffectNode, unwrapTcoExpr)
import Gopurs.ExprContext (ExprContext, ExprResult, TranslateExpr, StmtTree(..), flattenStmts)
import Gopurs.GoAst (GoExpr(..), GoType(..))
import Gopurs.GoConversions (boxGoExpr)
import Gopurs.ImmediateFfiEffects as ImmediateFfiEffects
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Codegen.Tco (TcoExpr(..))
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.CoreFn (ExprType(..), Ident)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.FreeVars (localId)
import PureScript.Backend.Optimizer.Syntax (BackendEffect(..), BackendSyntax(Abs, EffectDefer, Let, LetRec), Level)

bindEffect :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> Maybe Ident -> Level -> TcoExpr -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
bindEffect translate context nextId mbIdent lvl binding body =
  case ImmediateFfiEffects.direct translate context nextId mbIdent lvl binding body of
    Just result -> result
    Nothing -> ordinaryBind translate context nextId mbIdent lvl binding body

ordinaryBind :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> Maybe Ident -> Level -> TcoExpr -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
ordinaryBind translate context@{ codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr, bound, options: { isTail } } nextId mbIdent lvl binding body =
  let
    stripEffectDefer (TcoExpr a syn) = case unwrapTcoExpr (TcoExpr a syn) of
      EffectDefer inner -> let Tuple _ i = stripEffectDefer inner in Tuple true i
      Abs _ inner -> let Tuple _ i = stripEffectDefer inner in Tuple true i
      Let ident lvl_ val body_ -> let Tuple stripped i = stripEffectDefer body_ in Tuple stripped (TcoExpr a (Let ident lvl_ val i))
      LetRec lvl_ bindings_ body_ -> let Tuple stripped i = stripEffectDefer body_ in Tuple stripped (TcoExpr a (LetRec lvl_ bindings_ i))
      _ -> Tuple false (TcoExpr a syn)
    Tuple wasStripped realBinding = stripEffectDefer binding
    originalName = localId mbIdent lvl
    name = originalName <> "_" <> show nextId
    newBound = Map.insert originalName { name, goType: TypeValue } bound
    resBinding = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: true }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) (nextId + 1) realBinding
    resBody = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), bound = newBound, tcoIdent = Nothing, options = { isTail, inEffectBlock: true } }) resBinding.nextId body
    bindingExpr = if wasStripped then boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resBinding.expr resBinding.exprType else executeIfOpaque realBinding (boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resBinding.expr resBinding.exprType)
    bodyExpr = executeIfOpaque body resBody.expr
  in
    { stmts: resBinding.stmts <> StmtLeaf (GoAssign name bindingExpr) <> resBody.stmts, expr: bodyExpr, exprType: resBody.exprType, nextId: resBody.nextId }

pureValue :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
pureValue translate context@{ depth } nextId binding =
  translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId binding

defer :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
defer translate context@{ codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr } nextId binding =
  let
    resBinding = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: true }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId binding
    funcExpr = GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Func")
      [ GoFuncBlock [ Tuple "_" TypeValue ]
          (flattenStmts resBinding.stmts <> [ GoReturn (boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resBinding.expr resBinding.exprType) ])
          TypeValue
      ]
  in
    { stmts: StmtEmpty, expr: funcExpr, exprType: TypeValue, nextId: resBinding.nextId }

primitive :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> BackendEffect TcoExpr -> ExprResult
primitive translate context@{ codegenStateRef, depth, modNameStr } nextId eff =
  case eff of
  EffectRefNew a ->
    let
      resA = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId a
    in
      { stmts: resA.stmts
      , expr: GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "NewSTRef")
          [ boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resA.expr resA.exprType ]
      , exprType: TypeValue
      , nextId: resA.nextId + 1
      }
  EffectRefRead a ->
    let
      resA = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId a
    in
      { stmts: resA.stmts
      , expr: GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "ReadSTRef")
          [ boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resA.expr resA.exprType ]
      , exprType: TypeValue
      , nextId: resA.nextId
      }
  EffectRefWrite ref val ->
    let
      resRef = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId ref
      resVal = translate (context { depth = (depth + 1), tcoIdent = Nothing, loopCtx = [], options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: false }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) resRef.nextId val
    in
      { stmts: resRef.stmts <> resVal.stmts
      , expr: GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "WriteSTRef")
          [ boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resRef.expr resRef.exprType
          , boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr resVal.expr resVal.exprType
          ]
      , exprType: TypeValue
      , nextId: resVal.nextId
      }

wrap :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> ExprResult
wrap translate context nextId tcoExpr =
  let
    res = translate (context { options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: true }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId tcoExpr
  in
    { stmts: StmtEmpty, expr: boxedAction context res, exprType: TypeValue, nextId: res.nextId }

-- ModuleBindings calls this only for values initialized by a cached getter.
-- Match exactly the effect syntax wrap already defers: aliases, factories and
-- EffectDefer retain their existing construction/evaluation boundaries.
wrapCachedInt :: TranslateExpr -> ExprContext -> Int -> TcoExpr -> Maybe ExprResult
wrapCachedInt translate context nextId expression = do
  case getExprType expression of
    ADT "Effect.Effect" _ [ Int ] -> pure unit
    _ -> Nothing
  guard (isEffectNode expression)
  let
    result = translate (context { options = { isTail: false, inEffectBlock: true }, mbExpectedExprType = Nothing, mbExpectedGoType = Nothing }) nextId expression
    -- Translate once, retaining the original boxed body as an independent
    -- entry point. Each invocation executes exactly one of these bodies.
    nativeResult = case result.exprType, result.expr of
      TypeInt64, value -> Just value
      TypeValue, GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Int") [ value ] -> Just value
      _, _ -> Nothing
    action = case nativeResult of
      Just value ->
        let native = GoFuncBlock [] (flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoReturn value ]) TypeInt64
        in GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "WithFunctionData") [ boxedAction context result, native ]
      -- Boxed dynamic results retain the FFI's complete Unbox semantics.
      -- Reuse this translation even when it cannot provide a native entry.
      Nothing -> boxedAction context result
  pure { stmts: StmtEmpty, expr: action, exprType: TypeValue, nextId: result.nextId }

boxedAction :: ExprContext -> ExprResult -> GoExpr
boxedAction { codegenStateRef, modNameStr } result =
  GoCall (GoSelector (GoVar "gopurs_runtime") "Func")
    [ GoFuncBlock [ Tuple "_" TypeValue ]
        (flattenStmts result.stmts <> [ GoReturn (boxGoExpr codegenStateRef modNameStr result.expr result.exprType) ])
        TypeValue
    ]

# Generated-code review: effects, strings, sieve and TCO

The comparison contains6 changed sections among633 in core and8 among683 in all. Section counts and package placement are unchanged. All package headers, runtime Go, entry points, initialization order files, FFI sections, Bench and AppLibrary remain byte-identical. In particular the clock/batch adapter, benchmark registrations, C references and opaque FFI implementations are untouched. `effects-generated-functions.json` names the eight changed functions; its bounded extractor reads each packed file once and computes function spans once per selected section.

## Four selected targets

- `Test_EffectRefWrite10000.prepare`: preparation, opaque argument helper, captured opaque action and its replay remain in place. The selected positive-count branch now assigns the boxed integer directly. The cold branch executes the same Ref.new, writeEffect action and Ref.read calls in the same order, without constructing and immediately applying an intermediate closure. `Call_Test_EffectRefWrite10000_writeEffect` is byte-identical. The public getter corpus passes48 before and48 after observations with identical complete output, including saved captures and repeated invocations. Positive counts at/aboveInt32max are not run because that unchanged loop does not terminate there; the structural cold-worker equality documents this boundary.
- `Test_StringTakeCodePointsUnicode1500.prepare`: the two opaque inputs remain evaluated in their original order. The action now captures the closed fold callback, literal seed, count and native string, then scans at most count code points. Its ASCII fast branch and DecodeStringCodePoint fallback retain the existing UTF8/WTF8 contract; the intermediate take result and subsequent checksum call disappear. The original checksum worker and FFI take implementation remain unchanged. Count<=0 still captures inputs before returning the seed. Unicode/invalid-byte and cache evidence belongs to the independently validated CP.take proofs.
- `Test_Primes.__gopurs_list_progression_fold_0`: only the proved lower==2 path is added. It uses a local512-byte boolean buffer when the bounded prefix fits, an odd-only sieve starting atp² and final Int32 narrowing. The preexisting caller guards, opaque preparation and the general lower-bound path remain unchanged. Other lower bounds still use the prior2p algorithm.
- `Test_TCO.deepTailRec`: a closed arithmetic result for the recognized remainder recurrence is added under positiveInt32-count and canonicalInt32-seed guards. The previous narrowed loop and general fallback remain verbatim. Opaque inputs and the prepared action are unchanged; this is runtime algebra on the opaque count, not constant-input substitution.

## Other executable library changes

All four are consequences of the same immediate-effect-branch pass, in core and all. These are executable callback bodies, not merely setup formatting; callers which reach the generic helpers can benefit even though their own section is unchanged.

- `Get_Control_Monad_Rec_Class_monadRecEffect`: Loop still invokes the callback once, writes its result to the reference and yields false; Done yields true. Branch conditions, callback/Ref-write order and outer loop invocation are unchanged. Inner selected action closures and their immediate Apply are removed. An invalid constructor still raises the same pattern-match panic before any added outer Apply could execute.
- `Get_Control_Monad_ST_Internal_monadRecST`: the analogous Loop callback and WriteSTRef remain ordered; Done returns Unit. The outer ST loop and reference state transitions remain intact.
- `Call_Data_Array_ST_modify`: Just still computes f(value) and performs pokeImpl once; Nothing still returns false. The tag/nil tests and invalid-constructor panic remain. Only the selected action closure and immediate application disappear.
- `Call_Data_Array_ST_Iterator_pushWhile`: the Just/predicate condition still short-circuits. The successful branch pushes once, then performs the same iterator/ref callback. Its remaining nested callback is retained. The unknown/opaque break branch still constructs its action and applies it exactly once; that Apply moves inside its selected branch. No predicate, iterator factory or mutation is hoisted across the branch.

The generated source supports the intended attribution above. This review does not assign every measured change to these helpers merely because their definitions changed; official before/after measurements remain authoritative. No concat fusion is included in this wave.

## Validation and provenance

Ref source fixtures pass Release/Dev on both isolated JS and combined native compilers,32 exact source-JS observations per profile. Related/candidate unit suites pass19/19. The separate unsafePerformEffect-in-pure-let diagnostic is retained: baseline native, hook-disabled same-host and active outputs are identical to one another and differ from source JavaScript ordering. That existing discrepancy is documented, not fixed or hidden by adjusted expected values. The accepted saved-action fixture sequences construction explicitly in Effect.

No compiler/runtime/benchmark file was changed during review or corpus execution; the Ref corpus uses a separate Go overlay only for the generated scalar input helper.

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. # 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

ref-corpus/README.md.text:
# Public Effect.Ref action corpus

The runner imports the exact generated package from before-all or after-all; it does not regenerate the benchmark. A Go overlay changes only the generated cached scalar argument helper, supplying a varying Int64 input before the original opaque preparation worker. No benchmark source, FFI implementation, runtime file, prepared action or writeEffect worker is edited.

Twelve terminating inputs include Int64min, values below Int32min, negatives, zero, normal positives and Int32max-1. All twelve actions are prepared first. Each is then replayed four times in reverse input order while the overlay input is changed to an unrelated value. The same official adapter checks FunctionData[func()int64], then uses Unbox[int](Apply(action,Unit)); current actions follow the fallback ABI. This gives48 observations per stage and proves captured inputs survive later preparation and replay.

Positive counts at or above Int32max are not executed because the original write loop does not terminate there. The final generated-source review must check the cold worker/fallback separately. Original package/runtime hashes are checked before and after each run. This untimed correctness corpus supplies no performance result.

Commands from campaign directory:
`python3 proofs/ref-corpus/prepare.py before-all/output proofs/ref-corpus/before`
Then from that generated directory: `GOWORK=off go run -overlay overlay.json main.go > observations.json 2> run.log`.
Use after-all/output and proofs/ref-corpus/after for the identical after stage. Read result.json/manifests for completion and source guards.

campaign/core/README.before.md.text:
# 🌈 PureScript universal multi-runtime benchmark ## Project goal This project is a **proof of concept** demonstrating the power of abstraction and portability offered by **PureScript**. The goal is to show how the exact same pure functional code (without any manual FFI) can be compiled and executed natively on radically different ecosystems. Backends consume either standard `CoreFn` or, for the local AOT backends, the typed `TAST/tcorefn` representation exported by a local PureScript fork (may be subject to an official PR soon). ## Comprehensive benchmarks The benchmark suite runs a **wide variety** of computationally intensive tasks: AST evaluation, massive list processing, tail call optimization, deep record updates... These tests apply massive **pressure** on the call stack, garbage collector, disk I/O, event loops, and runtime execution engines to measure the raw ability of the compiler and the underlying virtual machine. > [!NOTE] > **Reading the benchmark tables** > > - **Status, only for gopurs, purust, phpurs, sharpurs and javapurs:** **Stable** = measured and considered fully optimized; **WIP** = measured, with optimization work remaining; **Backlog** = planned work without a published measurement or ratio. Status labels belong only to the relevant backend columns. References and external backends have no status. Stable is currently empty, including for Go: the available analyses still identify optimization opportunities. > - **Ratios:** `/C` uses the optimized imperative C reference; `/JS` uses the first JavaScript column. **Below 1× is faster; above 1× is slower.** Extended Results uses its own JS reference and has no C reference. > - **Totals:** sums of the available per-test medians: **Total WIP** for the controlled backends, **Total** for references and external backends. Backlog never contributes. Empty Stable groups are shown as *Coming soon...* and have no defined total, ratio or mean. These totals do not represent an application benchmark. > - **Summaries:** `μ` = arithmetic mean, `Q₂` = median, `G` = geometric mean of the case ratios. Each case has equal weight. All four ratios use exactly the same measured cases on both sides: Go/C and Go/JS both cover all 37 measured Go cases. The full total of a reference table is not used as a denominator for a different set of cases. Very small reference times can produce large ratios. > - **Missing data:** `—` means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Bounds (`< …`) are excluded from summaries. `n=a/b` indicates coverage: measured cases out of listed cases for a time total, or matched references out of measured cases for a ratio. Historical diagnostic measurements remain in the reference tables; their controlled-backend counterparts belong to unmeasured Backlog. > - **Display precision, in every table:** values ≥ 1 use two decimal places (`12.000045 → 12.00`); positive values < 1 keep two significant digits after leading zeros (`0.000045`, `0.009492 → 0.0095`). Zero is `0.00`. > - **Opaque inputs, in every table:** inputs must remain unknown to the optimizer at runtime. Algebraic simplification is allowed; substituting the driver’s known input is not. > - **Calculations:** use archived timings before display rounding, including for threshold checks. `≈` marks a fallback to published precision. ### Core stresstest benchmark results (pure computational) **Core tests (`src/`)** cover features common to all tested targets (`./bin/run`) #### JavaScript JS Benchmark | Hand-written PureScript

implementation-effects.md.text:
# Immediate execution of effect branches

The generic compiler change applies only to the continuation of `EffectExprs.ordinaryBind`, where the existing code immediately applies the selected action to Unit. A Branch with at least one syntactically known effect leaf can execute that leaf in its selected branch block. The known effect recognizer is unchanged. Explicit EffectDefer, unknown callbacks and factories retain their ordinary construction followed by one runtime Apply; saved branch values outside this consumer are not transformed.

ControlExprs.branchWith factors the existing branch generator to distinguish condition and body translators. Conditions keep the existing ordinary translator, evaluation order and short-circuit rules. Known bodies use the same context as EffectExprs.wrap: inEffectBlock=true, isTail=false, cleared expected types. Let/LetRec ending in a known effect inherit that context. Nested Branch nodes use the same transformation. Joins are boxed Value, identical to the original runtime Apply result; native leaves are boxed only at branch exit. Opaque leaves use ordinary inEffectBlock=false translation and one Apply. No descriptors, signatures, helper ABI, cache schema, FFI or runtime changes.

Initial isolated source build succeeds. Real frozen Effect.Ref write CoreFn compiled through the JS compiler: opaque preparation and captured replay action remain; the positive-count branch directly produces its Value; cold Ref.new/writeEffect/read remains in place. The actual registered getter passes twelve replays, and testing.AllocsPerRun through the official fallback adapter reports zero allocations, compared with one 32-byte allocation in the original paired diagnostic. No positive count at or above Int32max is executed because the original write loop is nonterminating there.

Targeted tests exercise admission/fallback, nested branches, condition short-circuit/order, unknown factory and effect once, repeated invocations, EffectDefer, panic identity, and Let/LetRec translator contexts. A separate source fixture compares JavaScript and generated Go traces for Release and Dev, including saved/replayed actions, effects returning actions, factories, and throwing conditions. Its final status is recorded separately after completion.

Scope: three compiler modules, two test runners, one PureScript fixture. The six frozen files were transferred after the next baseline and root approval; proofs/effects-transfer.json records base checks and hashes. Diagnostic numbers are not official Go/C measurements.

Final isolated validation: targeted branch tests2/2 PASS; source E2E2/2 PASS across Release and Dev with 32 output observations in each profile. The actual choose worker has exactly one outer action closure; selected pure/known branches no longer allocate an inner action. The unsafe-let diagnostic is archived separately in unsafe-let-order-diagnostic, with baseline-native, same-host hook-disabled and active outputs byte-identical. Its preexisting source-JS ordering difference is not corrected by this change. The accepted saved-action fixture sequences construction explicitly in Effect and compares exact unmodified JavaScript output.

Related suites plus targeted tests:19/19 PASS. Main transfer is complete; combined native E2E and official measurements remain separate pending phases. Archive probe-effects contains bounded sources/logs/oracles and the preceding raw CPU profile. Large diagnostic compiler bundles and dependency output trees are omitted; their hashes/paths remain in manifests.

Combined native validation is now complete: Release/Dev E2E2/2 PASS,32 exact source-JS observations per profile, protected sources/tests/bin/runtime unchanged. Public-action corpus48before+48after agrees byte-for-byte; only the generated input helper is overridden in a diagnostic Go overlay. The nonterminating positive fallback is excluded from execution and its original worker is structurally byte-identical. Generated review is in proofs/generated-other-modules-review.md.

implementation-codepoint-take.md.text:
# Codepoint take immediately consumed by a scalar fold

The candidate removes the temporary substring and codepoint array only when a canonical `Data.String.CodePoints.take count input` is immediately consumed by a known closed `String -> Int` codepoint fold. It does not change any benchmark, reference C program, runtime decoder or FFI implementation.

## Admission and fallback

`CodePointFold.describe` records a distinct `codePointFold` descriptor for a nonrecursive function with native String-to-Int ABI. The body must be the canonical `foldlArray callback literalSeed (toCodePointArray input)`, including the existing canonical composition exposure. The callback consists of exactly two Int arguments and closed scalar primitive expressions. Every available concrete TAST wrapper must agree, including lambda suffixes, primitive expressions and the canonical function heads. Unknown calls, effects, captures and contradictory annotations reject the descriptor.

`CodePointTakeFold` accepts only the canonical fully applied curried `take`; homonyms, hidden uncurried calls, stored substrings and unknown consumers retain ordinary code. Imported callback locals are freshened beyond the producer and descriptor scopes. The new path does not mutate input strings or rely on ownership/use-count annotations.

## Evaluation and arithmetic

The count expression is captured before the string expression and both still execute for zero and negative counts. The closed callback and literal seed have no creation effects. The bounded loop decodes at most the requested number of codepoints, reusing the existing ASCII fast path and exact UTF8/WTF8 decoder. The callback expression is emitted by the existing Int primitive lowering; all narrowing and multiplication behavior remain intact. Empty prefixes return the original seed, including native-wide seeds.

## Cache contract

`codePointFold` is distinct from `arrayFold`. Its contents and absence are included in imported worker metadata and emission keys. Workers use codec v4, while the physical cached fragment remains index 3. Previous v1/v2/v3 worker ownership remains readable for migration; typed worker reuse requires v4 and revalidates descriptor closure and ABI. Source E2E transitions change callback, then seed, then remove eligibility while retaining exactly the same native String-to-Int signature.

## Evidence and scope

The prior isolated probe is `go-string-take-fold-probe-20261127`: 8568 comparisons against actual native FFI take plus checksum; three timing repetitions in one process, median 7264 ns to 2956 ns and two allocations to zero. Those are diagnostic results, not this campaign’s official measurements. The original probe files are preserved unchanged.

The current candidate’s actual-workload smoke activates the imported descriptor and returns 64421000. Generated Go units cover 11235 bounded comparisons and 126 existing unbounded comparisons. The runtime corpus replays the unchanged real action through Apply, the actual measurement adapter and a forced generic fallback: 8316 observations per build, 1008 in the Node-comparable UTF16 domain and 7308 for historical native arbitrary bytes. These domains remain distinct and do not extend the C reference domain.

Final source E2E, native execution and campaign results are recorded in the manifests under `proofs`; only completed manifests support completion claims. The first isolated E2E attempt was stopped after cache tests caught a fragment-index migration typo; its logs are diagnostic only. The corrected candidate replays all relevant cache tests and source transitions before transfer.

Final validation completed: source JS and native compilers both pass Release/Dev with six cache transitions per host; all 21 observable logs are identical. # Crible : préfixe de nombres premiers

Le prépass ListProgressionFold existant reconnaît complètement la production d'un intervalle, l'élimination ordonnée des multiples de sa tête et le pliage entier. Une branche supplémentaire ne s'applique que lorsque la borne inférieure dynamique vaut 2. Les gardes existantes bornent alors la borne supérieure à 1 048 577, et la seed à Int32.

Cette branche exclut les pairs, marque les multiples impairs à partir de p² jusqu'à sqrt(upper), puis additionne les survivants. Un tampon local de 512 booléens couvre les petites entrées ; au-delà, une allocation reste autorisée. Les deux produits et la somme avant réduction finale tiennent en Int64 dans le domaine admis. Le repli pour lower>2 garde exactement son algorithme général : ces intervalles peuvent sélectionner des têtes composées, donc commencer systématiquement à p² serait incorrect.

La sonde utilise le helper réellement généré avant, des entrées opaques dynamiques et trois processus distincts : médiane 532,9→211,0 ns, 1 allocation→0. Ce ne sont pas les timings de l'App entière. Ses 1 102 cas comprennent 1 100 comparaisons contre un oracle indépendant par élimination de liste, plus deux grands préfixes contre l'ancien bitmap.

Les 23 tests ciblés passent, dont 1 085 comparaisons du Go généré contre l'oracle ordonné et sept bornes d'allocations. Le premier attendu d'une allocation exacte dans le petit repli général était trop strict : Go peut placer cette courte allocation dynamique sur pile ; l'échec initial est conservé, et le contrat vérifie le plafond d'une allocation, avec zéro obligatoire pour le chemin local. L'E2E JS Release/Dev passe avec résultats source identiques, bornes générales, grands intervalles, alias et callbacks inconnus. Revue indépendante de string_optimization : domaine, indices, somme et repli jugés cohérents.

Trois fichiers ont été transférés après contrôle main==baseline : module, tests IR et E2E existants. L'ajout ultérieur du champ codePointFold: Nothing par la passe CP.take est une insertion séparée, sans changement du corps du crible. Les preuves de l'exécutable final natif et les mesures officielles restent distinctes de ces sondes.

Validation finale : le compilateur natif combiné passe aussi les mêmes fixtures en Release et Dev. Les deux suites donnent quatre entrées Node, toutes correctes ; les 31 unités crible/TCO sur le JS combiné passent également. Les logs de phase et hashes du compilateur sont conservés dans proofs/loops-native-result.json. Ces contrôles complètent les preuves isolées, sans les compter deux fois.

implementation-tco.md.text:
# Récurrences scalaires et somme des restes

AffineLoops sait déjà réduire des récurrences scalaires de compte à rebours avec incrément constant, en préservant leur repli et les premières demandes de globals stricts. Cette extension admet aussi uniquement l'incrément `counter mod d`, avec un diviseur littéral positif Int32 et le même compteur que celui qui décrémente de 1 vers zéro. Aucun appel, diviseur dynamique, autre compteur, effet ou accès inconnu n'est admis.

Dans le domaine existant (compteur positif au plus MaxInt32, seed canonique), q=n/d et r=n%d donnent une somme des périodes q*d*(d-1)/2 + r*(r+1)/2. Les produits tiennent en Int64. La réduction finale Int32 est équivalente aux additions successives modulo 2³² ; elle ne remplace pas ces produits par IntMul, qui possède une sémantique Number. Les autres entrées conservent le corps précédent complet, y compris seed large et compteur zéro. Les demandes strictes restent ordonnées après la garde, sans changement de leur preuve d'admission.

La sonde copie le vrai worker TCO et conserve ses paramètres opaques : trois processus donnent 59 632→1,877 ns, zéro allocation de chaque côté. Cette réduction élimine algébriquement les itérations ; elle ne mesure pas un coût par itération et n'est pas un pliage d'une entrée connue. Les 1 032 cas de sonde comprennent 1 000 oracles itératifs et 32 limites.

Huit unités passent sur le compilateur isolé. Les nouveaux tests ajoutent 546 cas de Go généré et 42 refus de garde, avec sept diviseurs, débordements, graines int64 larges et comptes non canoniques terminants. Les petites entrées utilisent un oracle BigInt itératif ; les grandes utilisent l'identité indépendante sum(k)-d*sum(floor(k/d)). Les tests antérieurs d'incrément constant, demandes strictes, ordre et exceptions continuent de passer.

L'E2E source JS Release/Dev confirme les récursions globales/locales, zéro, débordement et effets non appelés. Le smoke réel de Test.TCO retourne 100000, active la formule et conserve l'action opaque ainsi que le repli à l'identique après normalisation des alias de package. Revue indépendante de string_campaign sans problème identifié. Deux erreurs du script d'extraction du smoke sont conservées comme erreurs de harnais.

Quatre fichiers ont été transférés après contrôle main==baseline : AffineLoops, ses unités et l'E2E strict-affine-reads avec sa fixture. Le corpus des exécutables finaux vérifie séparément 88 entrées TCO via les workers natifs et boxés, les entrées JSON étant lues à l'exécution. Les tests du compilateur natif combiné et la campagne officielle sont à enregistrer après bootstrap.

Validation finale : le compilateur natif combiné passe aussi les mêmes fixtures en Release et Dev. Les deux suites donnent quatre entrées Node, toutes correctes ; les 31 unités crible/TCO sur le JS combiné passent également. Les logs de phase et hashes du compilateur sont conservés dans proofs/loops-native-result.json. Ces contrôles complètent les preuves isolées, sans les compter deux fois.

+package gopurs_runtime
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"math"

+
+func TestBoxValueIdentityPreservesPayloadAndMetadata(t *testing.T) {
+	callback := Func(func(value Value) Value { return value })
+	withData := WithFunctionData(callback, "callback metadata")
+	values := []Value{
+		{}, Int(1 << 40), Float(math.Float64frombits(0x7ff8000000000042)),
+		StrWithCodeUnits("a😀", 3), Array([]Value{Int(1234)}),
+		RecordDict2("a", "b", Int(1), Int(2)), callback, withData,
+	}
+	for _, value := range values {
+		if got := Box(value); got != value {
+			t.Fatalf("typed Value identity: got %+v, want %+v", got, value)
+		}
+		if got := Box[any](value); got != value {
+			t.Fatalf("interface Value identity: got %+v, want %+v", got, value)
+		}
+	}
+	if metadata, ok := FunctionData[string](Box[any](withData)); !ok || metadata != "callback metadata" {
+		t.Fatal("Box discarded callback metadata")
+	}
+}
+
+func TestBoxScalarAndForeignRepresentations(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, sample := range []struct {
+		input    any
+		expected Value
+	}{
+		{int32(-2147483648), Int(-2147483648)}, {int64(1 << 40), Int(1 << 40)},
+		{int(1234), Int(1234)}, {false, Bool(false)}, {true, Bool(true)},
+		{math.Float64frombits(0x8000000000000000), Float(math.Float64frombits(0x8000000000000000))},
+		{math.Float64frombits(0x7ff8000000000042), Float(math.Float64frombits(0x7ff8000000000042))},
+	} {
+		if got := Box(sample.input); got != sample.expected {
+			t.Fatalf("%T: got %+v, want %+v", sample.input, got, sample.expected)
+		}
+	}
+	if got := Box(int64(1234)); got != Int(1234) {
+		t.Fatal("native int64")
+	}
+	if got := Box(int(1234)); got != Int(1234) {
+		t.Fatal("native int")
+	}
+	if got := Box(int32(1234)); got != Int(1234) {
+		t.Fatal("native int32")
+	}
+	for _, text := range []string{"", "a😀", "\xed\xa0\x80", "\xff"} {
+		if got := Box(text); got.Type != TypeString || got.StrVal() != text {
+			t.Fatalf("string %q changed", text)
+		}
+		if got := Box[any](text); got.Type != TypeString || got.StrVal() != text {
+			t.Fatalf("interface string %q changed", text)
+		}
+	}
+	type namedInt int64
+	type namedValue Value
+	var pointer *int
+	var mapping map[string]int
+	var channel chan int
+	for _, input := range []any{nil, pointer, mapping, channel, namedInt(1234), namedValue(Int(1234)), struct{ N int }{1234}} {
+		got := Box(input)
+		if got.Type != TypeAny || !reflect.DeepEqual(got.PtrVal(), input) {
+			t.Fatalf("foreign %T representation changed", input)
+		}
+	}
+	if got := Box(pointer); got.Type != TypeAny || got.PtrVal().(*int) != nil {
+		t.Fatal("typed nil pointer changed")
+	}
+	if got := Box(namedInt(1234)); got.Type != TypeAny || got.PtrVal().(namedInt) != 1234 {
+		t.Fatal("named integer became primitive")
+	}
+}
+

+	values := []Value{Int(1234), Str("hello")}
+	boxed := Box(values)

+	nested := Box([]any{int64(1234), []any{true, "x"}, values})

+		t.Fatal("recursive array conversion changed")

+	values[1] = Str("changed")
+	if ArrayAccess(ArrayAccess(nested, 2), 1).StrVal() != "changed" {
+		t.Fatal("nested native slice alias changed")
+	}
+	for _, input := range []any{[]Value(nil), []any(nil)} {
+		if got := Box(input); got.Type != TypeArray || ArrayLength(got) != 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("typed nil slice %T changed", input)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestBoxFunctionAdaptersRemainDeferredAcrossGC(t *testing.T) {
+	calls := 0
+	mark := func() { calls++ }
+	for _, sample := range []struct {
+		name     string
+		input    any
+		args     []Value
+		expected Value
+	}{
+		{"unit", func() { mark() }, nil, Value{}},
+		{"bool", func() bool { mark(); return true }, nil, Bool(true)},
+		{"int", func() int { mark(); return 1234 }, nil, Int(1234)},
+		{"int64", func() int64 { mark(); return 1 << 40 }, nil, Int(1 << 40)},
+		{"string", func() string { mark(); return "x" }, nil, Str("x")},
+		{"float", func() float64 { mark(); return -1.25 }, nil, Float(-1.25)},
+		{"value", func() Value { mark(); return Int(1234) }, nil, Int(1234)},
+		{"unaryValue", func(v Value) Value { mark(); return v }, []Value{Int(1234)}, Int(1234)},
+		{"unaryAny", func(v any) any { mark(); return v }, []Value{Int(1234)}, Int(1234)},
+		{"curried2", func(a any) func(any) any {
+			mark()
+			return func(b any) any { mark(); return IntAdd(a.(Value).IntVal, b.(Value).IntVal) }
+		}, []Value{Int(1200), Int(34)}, Int(1234)},
+		{"curried3", func(a any) func(any) func(any) any {
+			mark()
+			return func(b any) func(any) any {
+				mark()
+				return func(c any) any { mark(); return IntAdd(IntAdd(a.(Value).IntVal, b.(Value).IntVal), c.(Value).IntVal) }
+			}
+		}, []Value{Int(1200), Int(30), Int(4)}, Int(1234)},
+	} {
+		t.Run(sample.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			before := calls
+			function := Box(sample.input)
+			if calls != before {
+				t.Fatal("boxing invoked callback")
+			}
+			runtime.GC()
+			args := sample.args
+			if len(args) == 0 {
+				args = []Value{{}}
+			}
+			result := function
+			for _, arg := range args {
+				result = Apply(result, arg)
+			}
+			if result != sample.expected {
+				t.Fatalf("got %+v want %+v", result, sample.expected)
+			}
+			if calls-before != len(args) {
+				t.Fatalf("callback calls got %d want %d", calls-before, len(args))
+			}
+		})
+	}

+
+func TestBoxTypedNilFunctionsStillFailOnlyWhenApplied(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, input := range []any{(func())(nil), (func() bool)(nil), (func() int)(nil), (func() int64)(nil),
+		(func() string)(nil), (func() float64)(nil), (func() Value)(nil), (func(Value) Value)(nil),

+	}
+}
